title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Eswatini: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Eswatini: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Eswatini: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: Managing administrative, legal, and benefit arrangements during a serious or terminal illness in Eswatini involves coordinating medical documentation, incapacity planning, pension nominations, and document authentication across national institutions. Several central government ministry portals under the gov.sz domain are unavailable or unstable from external networks, so this guide relies on live official websites for the Judiciary of Eswatini, statutory pension funds, hospice services, the Hague Conference (HCCH), and verified EswatiniLII legislation.

steps.title: Medical Documentation, Palliative Care, and Capacity Records
steps.html:
• Obtain comprehensive medical reports, diagnostic summaries, and treatment plans from the attending hospital or specialist; detailed medical findings are mandatory if applying for work-related disability compensation or early medical retirement [4][5][9].
  • Contact Eswatini Hospice at Home in Matsapha for holistic palliative care, symptom support, and 24/7 on-call guidance for patients and family caregivers [10].
  • Review statutory mental health and decision-making procedures under the Mental Health Order, 1978 if progressive illness impairs legal capacity to sign financial or legal instruments [12].

steps.title: Powers of Attorney, Wills, and Estate Custody
steps.html:
• Execute a written Power of Attorney while legal capacity remains intact so an appointed agent can manage banking, property, or administrative transactions, noting that ordinary powers of attorney generally lapse upon loss of capacity unless court supervision applies [1].
  • Prepare and execute a formal written will satisfying the signature and witness formalities of the Wills Act, 1955 (Act 12 of 1955) [7].
  • Deposit the original will for safe custody with the Master of the High Court in Mbabane under Section 5 of the Administration of Estates Act, 1902, which maintains the statutory register of wills and supervises tutors, curators bonis (sections 21, 26, and 69 onwards), and future estate administration [1][2][8].

steps.title: Disability Benefits, Medical Retirement, and Beneficiary Nominations
steps.html:
• Private-sector contributors covered by the Eswatini National Provident Fund (ENPF) can review the Physical Disability Benefit Checklist and Mental Disability Benefit Checklist and file certified medical documentation for incapacity payouts [3][4][5].
  • Update the Eswatini National Provident Fund (ENPF) Nomination Form through the official forms portal so designated dependants are accurately recorded [3][6].
  • Public officers enrolled in the Public Service Pensions Fund (PSPF) can check eligibility for Forced Medical Retirement or Duty-Related Disability Benefits under Regulation 8 (which provides an additional impairment pension proportioned from 1/12 to 1/3 depending on the degree of impairment), and ensure registered PSPF nominees meet age and statutory rules [9][14].

steps.title: Practical Records and Future Estate Readiness
steps.html:
• Assemble an organized dossier holding the Eswatini Personal Identification Number (PIN) or national ID, marriage certificates, bank account records, insurance policies, title deeds, and any safe-custody receipt issued by the Master of the High Court [1][8].
  • Record clear notes on minor dependants, since assets due to minors are protected through the Guardian's Fund administered by the Master of the High Court under Section 96 onwards of the Administration of Estates Act [1][8].

steps.title: Document Authentication and Hague Apostille Rules
steps.html:
• Eswatini is a Contracting Party to the HCCH 1961 Hague Apostille Convention (in force since 6 September 1968 by succession), which means Eswatini public documents do not require consular embassy legalization for use in other Convention member states [11][13].
  • Present notarized powers of attorney, certified civil records, or authenticated medical certificates to Eswatini's designated Competent Authority, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation in Mbabane, for an Apostille under the Authentication of Documents Act, 1965 (Act 20 of 1965) [11][12].

contacts.name: Master of the High Court
contacts.note: High Court Building, Hospital Hill, P.O. Box 19, Mbabane; safe custody of wills, curatorship supervision, and estate administration.

contacts.name: Eswatini National Provident Fund (ENPF)
contacts.note: Lidlelantfongeni Building, Corner Martin and Ngwane Street, Manzini (Helpline 2508 5700); disability benefits and nomination forms.

contacts.name: Public Service Pensions Fund (PSPF)
contacts.note: 7th Floor, Ingcamu Building, Mhlambanyatsi Road, P.O. Box 4469 Mbabane H100 (Toll Free 800 2401); medical retirement and disability benefits.

contacts.name: Eswatini Hospice at Home
contacts.note: Matsapha; home-based palliative care with 24/7 on-call clinical support.

contacts.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
contacts.note: P.O. Box 518, Mbabane; designated HCCH 1961 Hague Apostille Competent Authority for Eswatini.
